summary: South Korea’s won jumped to a two-year high on Monday, supported by lower oil prices and heavy dollar selling by local companies.

title: China Agrees to Curb Hybrid Car Exports to EU
summary: The EU said China agreed to slash millions of hybrid car exports after talks that spanned trade, investment and intellectual property rights. Bloomberg's Minmin Low discusses the implications. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stock and Bond Futures Rise as Oil Extends Decline: Markets Wrap
summary: Stock and bond futures advanced as crude oil extended its decline, with traders looking past the latest attacks on Saudi Arabia that have threatened to widen the war in the Middle East.

summary: Reports from HCL Technologies Ltd. and Tech Mahindra Ltd. should give investors more clarity whether Tata Consultancy Services Ltd.’s earnings beat signaled a wider pickup in contracts for India’s IT sector.

title: Gov. Koike's Next Key Priorities for Tokyo
summary: Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike has spent the last decade driving transformative reforms—from pioneering climate initiatives and universal childcare support to guiding the metropolis through the COVID-19 pandemic and the 2020 Olympic Games. Looking to the future, Koike sits down with Bloomberg’s Shery Ahn at Bloomberg's Tokyo Studio to exclusively discuss her key strategic priorities. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Malaysia Budget Sees Consumer Names Emerge Winners, Analysts Say
summary: Consumer stocks are among the biggest beneficiaries of Malaysia’s spending plan for 2027, boosted by higher allocations to improve households’ purchasing power, according to analysts. Malaysian stocks rose as much as 0.4% on Monday, extending Friday’s gains.

title: Gold Edges Up as Lower Oil Prices Pare Rate-Hike Expectations
summary: Gold edged higher as sliding oil prices provided traders with some optimism that central banks could hold off on further interest rate hikes, while lower bond yields also lifted some pressure on the metal.

title: India’s Capital Braces for More Protests After Mass Detentions
summary: India is bracing for a third straight day of tensions in its capital, with opposition parties on Monday planning a march to the Supreme Court and a youth-led movement pressing ahead with protests over a contentious revision of voter rolls.

title: Korean Bond Rally Seen Faltering as Traders Brace for Rate Hikes
summary: A rally in South Korean bonds may prove fleeting as the effect of government-led measures to quell volatility fades and expectations of further monetary policy tightening build, according to strategists.

title: Bond Selloff May Mean Fewer Rate Hikes From Global Central Banks
summary: Bond markets are starting to do some of the lifting for central banks around the world by pushing up borrowing costs themselves, potentially reducing the number of benchmark interest-rate hikes needed to get inflation under control.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 12
summary: Oil dropped as traders weighed President Donald Trump’s claim of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, even as hostilities escalated across the Middle East.

title: Wrightson’s Crandall Ends Weekly Market Missives After 44 Years
summary: Lou Crandall, the Wrightson ICAP chief economist whose dispatches on Treasury financing and Federal Reserve operations became required reading across trading desks for nearly half a century, announced he’s ending his weekly commentary.

title: Saudi Airport Hit Again as Riyadh Set to Host Major Events
summary: Saudi Arabia’s main airport came under renewed attack from Houthi rebels, a day after a strike on the facility killed 12 people and heaped pressure on the Middle East’s biggest economy as it prepares to host major events that seek to boost foreign investment.

title: US Bond Traders Await CPI, Warsh For Insight on Fed’s Rate Path
summary: Bond traders are looking to the latest consumer-price inflation figures and a planned appearance by Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh for insight into how quickly the central bank will continue raising interest rates.

title: 'Windows of Opportunity' to End War in Ukraine, SACEUR Says
summary: NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe (SACEUR) General Alexus G. Grynkewich - the alliance's top military commander - says the alliance should increase support to Ukraine when they're hit by Russian hybrid attacks. On the "brutal" war, he said there are "windows of opportunity" to bring the conflict to an end and that the alliance should seize them where possible to bring both sides to the table. He made the comments in his first interview with Bloomberg TV's Oliver Crook in Warsaw on Sunday Oct. 11. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bookmarked: Stories That Caught Our Eye This Week
summary: Bloomberg hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo are on Bloomberg This Weekend for “Bookmarked,” sharing stories that caught their attention over the past week. The hosts discuss the reporting that piqued their interest and explain why those stories stood out from the week’s news. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Former US Envoy Warns of Wider Middle East Conflict
summary: Former White House Middle East Coordinator Brett McGurk tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the deadly attack on Riyadh's international airport underscores the growing threat from Iran-backed Houthi militants, while hardline leadership in Tehran complicates efforts to negotiate an end to the broader regional conflict. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, McGurk discusses his new book, Brink, which recounts negotiations to free the October 7 hostages, and warns that the Trump administration's Russian diesel agreement could undermine efforts to end the war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Globalization Defies a Decade of Populist Pushback
summary: Bloomberg News Senior Economics Writer Shawn Donnan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that globalization has continued to expand despite a decade of populist policies, tariffs and efforts to reshape international trade following Brexit and President Donald Trump's first election victory. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Donnan says growing cross-border investment, global supply chains and digital technology demonstrate that the world economy remains increasingly interconnected despite political resistance. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Riyadh Airport Attack, Trump To Ukraine: “Time To Get A New President”
summary:
The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York.

Joined by Jason Horowitz - NYT Former Rome Bureau Chief, William Taylor - Atlantic Council Eurasia Center Distinguished Fellow, Jennifer Lee - BMO Capital Markets Senior Economist, Brett McGurk - Fmr NSC Coordinator for the Middle East, Ravi Gupta - Author, “The Invisible List”, and Leslie Shedd - Rising Communications President. (Source: Bloomberg)
